opening.argument: The speaker’s focus is teaching viewers how to design and communicate service offers. She introduces the topic as creating offers that sell, promises a formula for thinking about them, and asks providers to identify the outcome a client would take away after investing time or money. Her advice about names, packaging, and marketable outcomes covers free, low-cost, and high-end offers. The income statement is presented as her retrospective account of advertising that led her to join a coaching school; the weight-loss outcomes and short-term pricing are hypothetical examples, not a current solicitation. She also acknowledges the limits of what one consulting session can accomplish.

citations.quote: creating no-brainer offers that sell and how to do that and how to think about them
I'll give you a little bit of a formula of how to think about it
what you need to ask yourself the question is when this person has spent this time or invested this money with me what is the outcome that they will have walked away from
at every single level that you're creating offers, free, low cost or high end, you need to have sexy, no-brainer offers and having them packaged and bundled with sexy names and marketable outcomes
